title: GroK-build v2 smoke matrix case (redteam runner, schema v1)
description: JSON schema (draft-07, self-contained) for one case file of the grok-build v2 smoke matrix (beads apex-ayl.21 / apex-ayl.22). Superset of the in-tree runner contract (smoke/redteam/run.py validate_case_file) plus the campaign additions: suite/tier/bead identity, declared MCP and tool calls with anti-vacuous premise pins, timeouts with the OTEL cold-start budget, env assumptions, retry policy for environmental transients, and scoring semantics (VACUOUS vs PASS/FAIL, per-assert wire evidence). The runner's hand-rolled validator must implement exactly the keyword subset used here: type, properties, required, items, enum, pattern, minimum, maximum, additionalProperties, anyOf, description. No external $refs, no $defs, no patternProperties.

schema_version.description: Case schema version. 1 = this schema. Pre-version case files (RT-C1..RT-M11, no schema_version) are accepted by the runner for back-compat but fail the NEW-case gate: every file added after the drop-in must carry schema_version=1.

id.description: Uppercase case id, unique across the case set (run dir name is the lowercased id). Conventions: RT-* = pre-v1 redteam cases; T21-* = .21 tool/MCP coverage cells; M5-*/M6-* = matrix rows; XW-* = cross-wire switch cells.

title.description: Human-readable one-paragraph statement of what the case proves, including the verdict semantics (which outcome is PASS, which is a FINDING, which is a defect). Existing cases set the bar: the title is the case's contract.

bead.description: Campaign bead id this case belongs to (e.g. 'apex-ayl.21'). Optional only for legacy pre-v1 files; required in practice for every schema_version=1 case (the NEW-case gate checks it).

suite.description: Case type in the matrix. wire-shape = model echo + backend path only (RT-M5/RT-M6 row asserts). tool-call = a real plain builtin tool round-trip. mcp-call = a real MCP server tool round-trip (codegraph). mcp-tool = one case exercising both (the .21 default for per-row coverage cells). cross-wire = mid-session ACP model switch across wire backends (RT-CROSSWIRE1/1B, RT-XREPLAY1/2 lineage). compaction = seeded auto-compact probe (RT-C3/COMP-3 lineage). salvage = truncation/400-recovery probe (XREPLAY-1 strip-retry lineage). recon = record-only case (never fails). session-resume = legacy/persisted-format session resume through a fresh binary (WS9-S11 lineage; S03/S11 remain filed under `salvage` until this enum lands — both cases already validate, no re-file owed).

tier.description: Matrix slice. slim = the .36 6-row gate set (runs every gate); full = full-catalog sweep cells (sign-off moments only, very last). Slim and full are two slices of ONE matrix: a full-tier case must use the same wire/assert vocabulary as its slim twin.

model.description: Session model id (exact catalog spelling). Required for driver=acp cases and for non-rows step cases; row-based cases (rows[]) may omit it. Must match an enabled row in the live ~/.grok/config.toml catalog at run time.

wire.description: Declared expected wire backend for the session model (the live config api_backend row value). Wire pins target the matching request path: /v1/responses | /v1/messages (both OBSERVED in campaign captures; rt-m5 row pins) | /v1/chat/completions (PREDICTED from base_url + endpoint convention; NO cc request has been captured to date — the T21-CC case keeps its where-filter path-agnostic and ratifies the observed path via a path_rec recon pin; RED-CLEARED promotion discipline). Declaring the wire also drives the runner's per-wire expectations (container shapes, count_wire_model_calls path list — gap G1).

driver.description: Driver mode. headless = one binary process per turn (-p/--resume/--output-format/--always-approve); ACP = one long-lived 'grok agent stdio' NDJSON-RPC session (promptId-correlated step machine). tool/MCP cells use headless (the proven vehicle: RT-M8 wire evidence; ACP would additionally need a session/request_permission responder the runner does not have yet — gap G7).

cwd.description: ABSOLUTE session working directory override (runner gap G4: currently the cwd is a hardcoded temp dir under the run dir). REQUIRED for mcp-call/mcp-tool suites whose MCP server resolves its project by the session cwd (codegraph uses the client rootUri / an explicit projectPath arg): point it at the indexed repo (e.g. the worktree root containing .codegraph/). The runner launches the binary there read-only; it never writes the tree. The MCP server process itself must be hermetic (runner injects --no-watch for codegraph — gap G12) so the file watcher cannot write .codegraph/ during a case.

config_patch.description: Dotted section/key -> scalar patches applied to the COPIED live config.toml in the hermetic home (applied after the harness-invariant features/turn_summary=false patch, so a case can re-enable it). Values must be TOML scalars (bool/int/float/string); arrays/objects are rejected by the runner validator.

seed.description: History seeder (R-2 pinned chat_history.jsonl schema): pre-seed a session with synthetic history so compaction/truncation thresholds fire deterministically. Only for compaction/salvage suites.

hist_tokens.description: Target estimated tokens of the seeded history (4 chars/token heuristic).

hist_bytes.description: Target byte size of the seeded history; takes precedence over hist_tokens when both are set.

output_format.description: Headless --output-format value (ndjson pseudo-event stream the assert.ndjson ops evaluate). Ignored for driver=acp (fmt is forced to 'acp').

agents_json.description: Optional --agents JSON (echo/agent definitions for headless turns; RT-M5-era subagent cells).

watchdog_s.description: Per-turn watchdog timeout in seconds (step timeout_s overrides per step). Default 300 = the in-tree watchdog default; MCP-carrying cells keep 300 (cold MCP init is 7-30s per B-ii desync forensics; codegraph_explore on a 3.2k-file index is seconds).

est_calls.description: Estimated model-call cost of the case, used by the runner budget gate (budget.used + est_calls > --budget => SKIP). tool/MCP cells cost ~2 calls per tool-bearing turn (call turn + answer turn) + 1 per plain turn + side calls.

wirecap.description: Enable wiretap loopback capture for this case (the per-request wire evidence is how the campaign proves claims; scored cases keep it true). runner --no-wirecap still wins globally.

disabled.description: When true the case is SKIPped with reason/unblocks_at as the skip note (disabled cases are still schema-validated by the offline gate).

reason.description: Why the case is disabled (paired with disabled=true).

unblocks_at.description: Bead/condition that re-enables the case (paired with disabled=true).

recon.description: Record-only case: every assert is recon-class (always records, never fails); the row reports RECON instead of PASS/FAIL.

expected_red.description: Pre-registered red (RT-M1 lineage): a case whose FAIL is the expected evidence for a known defect. FAIL -> RED-EXPECTED(id), PASS -> RED-CLEARED(id) (promote the pin to a hard assert).

id.description: The finding/bead id the red is registered against.

tolerant.description: Tolerant-verdict flag (CROSSWIRE-1 / rt-xreplay1 discipline): when true, a scored-pin FAIL is reported as FINDING (the row is FINDING-PASS with the failed pin listed as a finding) instead of FAIL, and the title must enumerate which outcomes are acceptable findings vs defects. Use only where the acceptance claim is 'the rejection is recovered / the shape is recorded', never to hide a dead turn.

mcp_calls.description: DECLARED expected MCP tool calls (bead .21): each entry is a contract that this case must produce a real round-trip to a real MCP server tool — not a wire-shape assert about tool definitions. The runner scores them in two stages: premise (control) pins first (did the server announce / did the model call it?), then shape pins (did the round-trip close with the right wire shape?). An mcp-call/mcp-tool suite case with an empty mcp_calls is rejected by the NEW-case gate.

tool_calls.description: DECLARED expected plain builtin tool calls (bead .21): the per-model tool-path coverage. Same two-stage scoring as mcp_calls. A tool-call/mcp-tool suite case with an empty tool_calls is rejected by the NEW-case gate. Canonical plain tool: run_terminal_command with a write-free command (echo NONCE) — idempotent, no network, no worktree writes.

steps.description: Ordered step machine (mutually exclusive with rows). ACP driver: steps run inside ONE session (promptId-correlated). Headless driver: each turn/switch step is one binary process (-m/-p, --resume chaining for session steps).

rows.description: Row-based matrix case (headless only, RT-M5/RT-M6 shape): one fresh headless turn per row, scored by row_asserts (per-row where-filters so nth resolves within the row's own requests). runner --rows a,b filters which rows execute (the case file is the universe).

model.description: Exact catalog model id for this row.

prompt.description: Row prompt (default in runner: 'Reply with exactly: HT1-OK').

assert.description: Case-level assert block, evaluated after all steps/rows. Lists are independent; order is presentation only. Every scored assert SHOULD carry an 'id' (required for any pin named in scoring.vacuous_if) and a 'label' (the label is the assert's contract, copied into the report).

ndjson.description: Asserts over the merged ndjson pseudo-event stream (headless output or ACP synthesized events).

artifact.description: Asserts over session-dir artifacts (chat_history.jsonl, compaction_requests/, ...; copied under <case>/session/ in the report).

wire.description: Asserts over the wiretap captures (<case>/wire/req-NNN.json + resp-NNN.jsonl). The per-request wire evidence is first-class: every scored wire assert records its matched file(s) + request n in the report row.

exit.description: Expected final process exit code (honest-failure pins, e.g. exit=1 for the OVERCAP-1 turn-death class).

row_asserts.description: Row-based cases only: per-row wire asserts. Each entry is scoped to a row via row_model (legacy, takes precedence) or where['$.body.model'] (preferred form, RT-M6 regeneration); the runner evaluates it once per executed row, scoping nth to that row's own requests (default nth=0 = newest of the row). A row not executed (--rows filter) yields a wire.row-skip recon record.

timeouts.description: Timeout budget block (apex-ayl.32 cold-window strategy). Every ACP-facing budget is case-visible because the 424 BPS cold window (EDR/auditd per-syscall heat + 30s OTEL fleet-policy startup wait) makes fixed budgets environment-sensitive: the 26,001B init line takes 61.3s at the plateau (in-tree fix: 180s init + chunked read; 2.94x margin).

acp_init_s.description: ACP initialize + session/new budget (in-tree ACP_INIT_TIMEOUT_S=180). Raise for first-in-cold-window cells (e.g. 240) when the run is the first ACP launch after a machine cool-down.

acp_set_model_s.description: ACP session/set_model budget. The in-tree value is hardcoded 60 (run.py:981) — a gap (G6): 60s is inside the 424 BPS plateau budget for a 26KB-class response; the schema default is 180 and the drop-in makes the in-tree constant case-overridable.

turn_s.description: Per-turn watchdog (aliases the case-level watchdog_s when that is set; this field wins when both are present).

mcp_startup_s.description: Expected MCP server startup budget (binary default 30s per mcp_servers startup_timeout_sec). Informational for the harness-premise control pin: a case whose MCP announcement never lands inside turn 1's budget is BLOCKED/HARNESS, not VACUOUS.

retry.description: Environmental-transient retry policy (B-ii run-1 lesson: a transient qwen model-group 404 recovered <5min; 404 != model-bound 400). Retries the WHOLE case with a fresh hermetic home. NEVER retries a model-bound 400: a 400 with a schema/model-bound error body is the assertion surface (XREPLAY-1: the 400 is the probe).

on_status.description: HTTP statuses that mark a turn ENV-TRANSIENT when they are the LAST response for the row model (404 model-group flap, 502/503 proxy hiccups).

max_attempts.description: Extra full-case attempts after the first failure (0 = no retry, the in-tree behavior; the .22 runner default for slim-gate cells is 1).

recheck_models.description: Before retrying, re-list GET /v1/models through the wiretap: if the model id is GONE from the catalog the 404 is a catalog change, not a flap -> the case FAILs (a matrix signal) instead of retrying.

scoring.description: Scoring semantics block (the B-ii anti-vacuous rule). The runner evaluates premise (control) pins FIRST: a control pin that finds no expected artifact means the probe's premise did not hold. premise class model -> the row is VACUOUS (the probe is meaningless for this model; recorded with the 0-hit evidence, NOT PASS and NOT FAIL — this is the rt-xreplay2/B-ii behavior promoted from label to status). premise class harness -> the row is BLOCKED (the test rig failed: server never announced, binary missing; no model conclusion). A control pin that passes lets the scored pins decide PASS/FAIL. Both a control miss AND a scored fail -> FAIL (a real defect dominates a missing premise; the report lists both).

vacuous_if.description: Premise (control) pins: asserts whose 0-hit flips the row out of PASS/FAIL. Each names an assert id (an 'id' on a wire.grep/field/count or ndjson assert, or an mcp_calls/tool_calls entry id).

pin.description: The assert id (or mcp_call/tool_call id) acting as the premise control.

class.description: model = the MODEL did not produce the premise artifact (tool/MCP round-trip never issued) -> VACUOUS (temperament or capability gap; recorded, retriable under retry.policy only for env classes). harness = the RIG did not produce the premise (MCP server never announced on the wire) -> BLOCKED/HARNESS.

note.description: One-line statement of what premise this pin guards (copied into the report next to the VACUOUS/BLOCKED verdict).

require_wire_evidence.description: Every scored (non-recon) assert that PASSes must cite its wire evidence: the report row carries per-assert {evidence_file, request_n} for wire asserts and {event_line} for ndjson asserts. A PASS with an uncitable scored wire assert is downgraded to BLOCKED/NO-EVIDENCE by the report writer (the campaign proves claims by per-request wire evidence; a claim without a file is not a claim).

env.description: Declared environment assumptions of the case (the L1 env contract + wire-level invariants). The runner records the effective values in the report header; a mismatch between declaration and observation is a report anomaly (e.g. a case declaring store=false while a captured request carries store=true is a wire-shape finding).

store.description: Expected 'store' field on /v1/responses requests (the deployment runs store=false: reasoning items are NOT persisted upstream — the Azure rejection class 'items are not persisted when store is false', XREPLAY-1 pin (3/3)).

home.description: GROK_HOME mode. hermetic = tempdir copy of the live config with the harness invariants (turn_summary off, base_url rewritten to wiretap, aligned models_cache) — the in-tree default; new sessions never touch ~/.grok. temp = a bare temp home (only for rig-level cells that must not inherit the live catalog).

launcher.description: Which launcher drives the binary: runner = smoke/redteam/run.py (the .22 target); dogfood = ~/.grok/bin/grok-dogfood (v2 staged launcher: env -u provider vars, GROK_AUTH_EXPIRED=1, RUST_LOG scope, optional wirecap). Declared for provenance; the runner records the effective one.

provider_vars_unset.description: Provider env vars the launcher must UNSET (L1 env contract: ambient CODEX_LLM_PROXY_KEY only, never a second provider identity).

mcp_call.description: One declared MCP tool call. Scoring: (1) announcement control — the server's 'MCP server connected' system-reminder must appear on the session wire (harness premise); (2) call control — a function_call/tool_use with name use_tool targeting the qualified tool must appear (model premise, unless via=direct); (3) shape pins — the round-trip closes (a function_call_output / tool_result / tool-role message carrying the result) on the declared wire shape.

id.description: Case-unique id for this declared call (nameable in scoring.vacuous_if).

server.description: MCP server name exactly as configured in [mcp_servers.<name>] (e.g. 'codegraph').

tool.description: MCP tool name as exposed by the server (e.g. 'codegraph_explore').

expect_name.description: The fully-qualified name the use_tool call must target (server__tool, e.g. 'codegraph__codegraph_explore'). Defaults to server + '__' + tool when omitted.

via.description: How the binary surfaces the MCP tool. search_tool_use_tool = the current shape: MCP tools are NOT in the request tools[] array; the server's tools arrive as turn-boundary <system-reminder> announcement appends and are invoked via the builtin search_tool (BM25 discovery) + use_tool (fully-qualified target). direct = a future/alternate shape where the MCP tool is inlined into tools[] and called by its bare name — only valid when the model-config audit confirms the binary change.

args.description: Expected call arguments (informational contract + the prompt text is generated from them by the drop-in case template). For codegraph_explore: {query: <symbols/file names>, maxFiles?: int, projectPath?: <abs path of the indexed repo>}.

premise.description: Premise class of the CALL control pin (announcement is always harness-class). model: the model chose not to call the tool -> VACUOUS. harness: the rig could not offer the tool (e.g. via=direct on a binary that still defers MCP tools) -> BLOCKED.

output_contains.description: Substring that must appear in the tool result payload of the round-trip (e.g. a symbol name from the codegraph answer). A shape pin: 0 hits = FAIL (the call happened but returned nothing useful — server error, empty index, or model passed wrong args).

tool_call.description: One declared plain builtin tool call (the per-model tool-path coverage). Scoring: call control (a function_call/tool_use with the declared tool name appears on the wire — model premise) then shape pins (the round-trip closes with a matching output on the declared wire shape).

tool.description: Builtin tool name exactly as advertised in the request tools[] array (from the 31-name inventory: run_terminal_command, read_file, search_replace, list_dir, grep, write, todo_write, ...). Canonical choice: run_terminal_command with a write-free echo command.

args.description: Expected call arguments (e.g. {command: 'echo T21-...-ECHO'}). The command must be idempotent and write-free (no worktree writes, no network): the matrix may run with cwd set to the live worktree.

premise.description: Premise class of the call control pin. Plain builtin tools are always offered by the binary, so a missing call is a model-temperament VACUOUS, never harness.

output_contains.description: Substring that must appear in the tool result (e.g. the echo nonce). A shape pin: proves the round-trip carried the real output back to the model.

step.description: One step of the case step machine (in-tree STEP_OPS: turn, switch, switch_model, kill, compact, idle, recon_note). The ACP driver correlates every turn's completion by client-chosen promptId (apex-ayl.28; the prompt_id of each acp_turn is recorded in the report turns[]).

prompt.description: turn: the prompt text. The drop-in template appends the declared mcp_calls/tool_calls instruction block so the prompt and the contract cannot drift.

model.description: turn (optional, defaults to the case model) / switch (required) / switch_model (required): target model id.

via.description: switch / switch_model: acp = session/set_model inside the ACP session; resume = headless --resume a new session of the target model.

cell.description: switch_model: the XW-FIXTURES cell under smoke/xwfix/cells/ (e.g. 'smoke/xwfix/cells/az-vxm'). The fresh session is seeded with <cell>/pre_switch.json VERBATIM — headless: at case start (each turn process re-reads chat_history.jsonl at start, the proven seeder ordering); ACP: the cell is materialized under the session/new-minted session dir and then routed through session/load, because the actor loads ONLY summary.json at session/new and does NOT re-read chat_history.jsonl at the first prompt (persistence init_session; first-hand verified, 2026-09-17 ratchet ① adjudication) — session/load is the path that puts the seeded history in memory before the first prompt. The op then scores the storage-form cell diff AT SWITCH TIME (persisted chat_history.jsonl vs <cell>/expected.json) so the post-switch turn cannot contaminate the pin.

assert_form.description: switch_model: which cell form the op scores for the first captured request to the target model. storage (default) = the storage-form diff at switch time (the active RED — expected.json byte pin). wire = the WIRE-FORM byte pin: the first post-switch request to the target model is scored through the golden-kind compare engine against <cell>/expected_wire.json (canonical full-body compare — one engine; the retired cell_diff kind). The wire form is active for a cell once its expected_wire.json byte pin lands (scored even when assert_form=storage) and is skipped with a note until then.

kill_after_s.description: turn: kill the process after N seconds (tools-dark probes, RT-S2 shape).

expect_kill.description: turn: true (default) = a kill is the expected terminal (no FAIL); false = a kill FAILs the case.

s.description: idle: seconds to sleep (long-idle resume probes, RT-R3 shape).

note.description: recon_note: free-text note appended to the report turns[].

ndjson_assert.description: Assert over the merged ndjson pseudo-event stream (in-tree check_ndjson ops: count, absent, present, eq, ne, text_contains, tools_absent, tools_present, recon).

id.description: Assert id (nameable in scoring.vacuous_if; required on control pins).

event.description: Event type to match (count/absent/present/eq/ne): acp_error, acp_end, acp_message, end, available_commands, ...

which.description: eq/ne: which matching event to read the field from.

field.description: eq/ne: dot path into the event (e.g. 'stopReason', 'data.sessionId').

value.description: text_contains: substring the merged text must contain; eq/ne: the expected (or forbidden, for ne) value.

names.description: tools_absent/tools_present: tool names checked against the union of all advertised tool lists (available_commands).

absent_ok.description: present: absence is accepted ONLY on an error terminal (the honest-failure pin shape; a silent no-terminal run still FAILs).

label.description: The assert's contract in one paragraph (copied into report.md). Control pins use the 'CONTROL (anti-vacuous pin): ...' convention.

artifact_assert.description: Assert over session-dir artifacts (in-tree check_artifact: glob + count, grep, JSON field eq/ne/ne_null). Artifacts are copied into the report under <case>/session/ (chat_history.jsonl, summary.json, events.jsonl, compaction*, subagents).

op.description: Omitted op = JSON-field read of the first/last matched file.

file.description: Glob relative to the session dir (e.g. 'compaction_requests/*.json').

ne.description: Field must differ from this value.

grep.description: op=grep: substring to count across all matched files.

wire_assert.description: Assert over wiretap captures (in-tree check_wire kinds: field, grep, size_lt, count, resp_status, recon, golden). PIN FORMS and the count-tolerance lesson: 'nth' selects within the WHERE-FILTERED set sorted by capture time (nth=0 = NEWEST); a static nth breaks when the actual match count N differs from the pin's assumption (the B-i case bug: nth:1 out-of-range at N=1 -> case FAIL that was a case bug, not a product defect). Count-tolerant forms: 'any: true' = passes if ANY matched file matches (fail-closed on an empty set — the anti-vacuous default for premise/control pins), 'last: N' = Nth-from-oldest (nth = len-1-N), and a companion 'count' assert (min/max) that makes nth selections unambiguous (XREPLAY-1's 'exactly two requests' pin). Rule for new cases: NEVER pin a static nth >= 1 without a sibling count assert that bounds N; premise pins use any: true. kind=golden = the declarative WIRE-FORM byte pin: the selected capture's FULL request body, canonically serialized and normalized per the 'normalize' list, must equal the 'golden' fixture — the one compare engine, also called by the switch_model op's wire hook (R1C: the retired cell_diff is NOT a kind; the op scores its storage form itself and its wire form through this golden compare).

id.description: Assert id (nameable in scoring.vacuous_if; required on control pins).

file.description: Glob of capture files relative to <case>/wire/ (req-*.json for requests, resp-*.jsonl for responses).

golden.description: kind=golden: fixture path relative to <case>/wire/ (the same base the 'file' glob resolves against). The fixture is the EXPECTED request body as a JSON document — the capture's full 'body', not a body.input extraction — authored AFTER normalization (an explicit null at every position the 'normalize' paths hit). Compare: canonical JSON of the selected capture's full request body (json.dumps sort_keys + compact separators — object key order insensitive; list order SIGNIFICANT: the input[] conversation order is semantic and projection must not reorder it, so no order-insensitive list normalization exists) vs the fixture, after the 'normalize' paths are nulled in the capture. Selection reuses the count-tolerance machinery exactly (nth=0 newest, last:N, any:true fail-closed on an empty set) — keep the companion 'count' assert that bounds N (the B-i lesson) and the 'where' scope (G10: where is REQUIRED on this scored kind). On mismatch the assert FAILs with a structured field-level diff (first 5 diverging canonical paths with got/want snippets) written to the case report dir — the diff is the TDD RED artifact.

normalize.description: kind=golden: dotted paths (capture-root-relative, e.g. 'body.input.0.id', 'body.prompt_cache_key') whose values are nulled in the capture BEFORE the canonical compare. For per-run volatile values only (session-derived keys, upstream-issued ids); absent paths are a no-op; the fixture carries the matching explicit nulls. Do NOT use normalize to hide semantic drift — the drift is what the pin exists to catch.

where.description: Filter applied to each candidate request body BEFORE nth/any selection: JSON-path keys (bare 'method', 'path', dotted 'body.model'; '$.' prefix accepted) mapped to scalars, or to {prefix: str} / {not_prefix: str} for prefix matching (COMP-3: distinguishing xai-compact-* tagged requests). REQUIRED on every scored wire assert — unscoped filters catch the grok-4.6 session-title side call (.29: it lands on /v1/responses in every ACP run and 500s proxy-side) and any other foreign request. Session scoping: the capture carries the client session id in the header 'headers.x-grok-session-id' (observed on every authenticated request across the report tree) — pin that key in 'where' whenever a foreign session's same-shape request could land in the same capture dir (parallel hermetic runs; the cross-session form of the side-call lesson).

path.description: kind=field: dot path into the request JSON (e.g. '$.body.model', '$.path').

ne.description: kind=field: value that must NOT be at path.

grep.description: kind=grep: substring over the file's raw text. kind=recon: the line-filter for the recorded slice. Captures are pretty-printed JSON (2-space indent), so grep JSON shapes with the spaced form: '"name": "use_tool"', '"type": "function_call_output"'.

absent.description: kind=grep: true = the substring must be ABSENT from the selected file(s) (the negative pin; with any: true it means 'no matched file carries it').

nth.description: Selection index into the filtered, time-sorted set (0 = newest). See the count-tolerance lesson in the kind description.

last.description: Selection Nth-from-OLDEST (equivalent to nth = len-1-N in the newest-first sorted set: last:0 = oldest filtered request, last:N-1 = newest); mutually informative with nth for the 1-vs-2 request tolerant-verdict cases. Doc corrected 2026-09-17 (was 'Nth-from-newest'; the code is nth=len-1-N with nth=0=newest).

any.description: true = pass if ANY filtered file matches (grep presence, or the absent=absent form); fail-closed on an empty filtered set. The standard form for premise/control pins.

all.description: true = the grep must be ABSENT from every filtered file (MA-3 form); requires absent:true (rejected without it); an empty filtered set is a fail-closed harness failure. Complement of any:true.

row_model.description: Row-based cases only (legacy form): exact catalog model id scoping this wire assert to one row's requests. Preferred form: scope via where['$.body.model'] (RT-M6 regeneration); the runner accepts both (row_model takes precedence).

min.description: kind=count: minimum number of filtered files (e.g. NO-RETRY-STORM pins: min 1 max 2).

max.description: kind=count: maximum number of filtered files.

which.description: kind=resp_status: which filtered request to look up the response for (default = the capture-order first = oldest; 'last' = the final request of the tolerant-verdict pair).

status_in.description: kind=resp_status: acceptable HTTP statuses for the paired resp-NNN.jsonl (e.g. [200]).

max_bytes.description: kind=size_lt: the selected file must be smaller than this many bytes (salvage/truncation budget pins).

base.description: kind=recon: glob base dir (wire captures or the session copy).

label.description: The assert's contract in one paragraph. Control pins use the 'CONTROL (anti-vacuous pin): ...' convention; the recon verdict pin uses the 'VERDICT RECORD' convention with a disclosure of any parallel side call that may land newest.

field.description: kind=recon only: path (get_path form) of the value to record from the selected capture file, e.g. '$.path' (runner check_recon field extraction).

op.description: kind=recon alternative form: op=recon + what=final-text records the ndjson final-text head without a capture file (runner check_recon).

event.description: kind=recon alternative form: record the field of the LAST ndjson event of this type (runner check_recon event form).

value.description: kind=recon literal value form: record this constant as the verdict record (runner check_recon).
